findings.statement: CA9 protein is strongly up in tumour (log2FC 2.269), with RNA, protein and phospho layers all concordant. It is rank 1 in the convergence ranking and has antibody drugs in clinical development (girentuximab).

CA9 RNA is massively up in tumour (log2FC 6.312, 75 pairs), consistent with HIF activation after VHL loss; the RNA signal is tumour-intrinsic by the purity check and replicates in TCGA-KIRC, but it is not prognostic there.

CD70 is a membrane target with protein up in tumour (log2FC 2.421) and RNA also up. It has anti-CD70 agents in clinical trials (cusatuzumab, vorsetuzumab mafodotin), is tumour-intrinsic by purity and replicates in TCGA, with no prognostic signal.
ENPP3 is a surface enzyme with protein up in tumour (log2FC 1.544) and RNA up; it is tumour-intrinsic by purity and has the antibody-drug conjugate AGS-16C3F (phase 2) as precedent.

SCARB1 (HDL receptor) ranks first in the target profile; protein is up in tumour (log2FC 1.837) with concordant RNA and phospho layers, replicated in TCGA, and with an Open Targets genetic association. No drugs are recorded.

NNMT protein is up in tumour (log2FC 2.709) with concordant RNA. It is tumour-intrinsic, replicated in TCGA, and prognostic there (higher expression is linked to worse survival); it ranks first for the biomarker profile among up-regulated genes.

SLC16A3 (MCT4 lactate exporter) protein is up in tumour (log2FC 2.279), with RNA and phospho concordant. It is tumour-intrinsic and a plausible metabolic target; no DepMap dependency was seen in the ranking.

PSAT1 is the top-ranked biomarker candidate. Its protein is down in tumour (log2FC -1.963) with RNA also down and TCGA replication; lower expression is associated with a worse prognosis in TCGA. It is a biomarker, not a target.

ALDOB RNA is very strongly down in tumour (log2FC -7.028), reflecting loss of proximal-tubule identity. Protein and phospho are also down, it replicates in TCGA and low expression is associated with worse survival. It is a diagnostic or prognostic biomarker, not a target.
UMOD is a normal-tubule marker, down in tumour at the RNA and protein layers and replicated in TCGA; it signals loss of normal tubule identity and is not a target.

VHL is the dominant recurrent somatic driver in the combined CPTAC and TCGA cohort, mutated in close to half of patients [gene=VHL; type=somatic_recurrence; source=DATASET:SOMATIC-CPTAC-TCGA; freq=0.4834]. This is the disease driver mechanism behind HIF-dependent induction of CA9, NNMT and SLC16A3.

VHL copy-number loss is frequent on the 3p arm and has a real dosage effect on its RNA [gene=VHL; type=cis_dosage; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-CNV; arm=3p; rna_rho=0.506], which is significant [gene=VHL; type=cis_dosage; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-CNV; arm=3p; rna_padj=2.49e-7]. This distinguishes it from passenger losses.

caveats: Cohort of 110 tumours with 75 matched RNA normals and 84 proteome normals; bulk tissue, so stromal and immune genes (e.g. FCER1G, TYROBP) are susceptible to infiltration artefacts and were not prioritised.
Strongly down-regulated genes (ALDOB, UMOD, PSAT1) reflect loss of tubule identity and are biomarker candidates only.
DepMap dependency values are near zero for the top up-regulated candidates, so none has demonstrated essentiality; tractability is inferred from surface localisation and existing drugs.
Statements deliberately cite a single metric per record; other layer values (TCGA, purity, survival) should be checked against the cited gene-specific records.
Convergence scores are deterministic rankings with robustness intervals, not statistical tests.
